pr_title: Ensure platform setup for all AVM FRITZ!SmartHome devices
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
In case when one platform setup is delayed (_example https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/105346#issuecomment-1848942175_) the `coordinator.new_devices` might already be cleared by a meanwhile further coordinator data update run.
To ensure each platform is at proper set up, we statically run `_add_entities` with the whole bunch of devices during setup, but during coordinator update listener, we only consider the `coordinator.new_devices` property.

issue_context.title: AVM FRITZ!SmartHome sensor entities of Fritz DECT 200 are missing after update to 2023.12
issue_context.body:
### The problem

After I updated to Home Assistant 2023.12 the sensor entities of my Fritz DECT 200 device are no longer provided by the integration. The missing sensor entities are:
- sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_total_energy
- sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_power_consumption
- sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_temperature
- sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_voltage
- sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_electric_current

They are still available in the Fritz!Box UI.


The following entities of this device are still available and working in the integration:
- switch.fritz_dect_200_1
- binary_sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_button_lock_on_device
- binary_sensor.fritz_dect_200_1_button_lock_via_ui

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.12.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.11.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

AVM FRITZ!SmartHome

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fritzbox/

### Diagnostics information

My `command_line` sensors are working fine. Under normal circumstances the commands take only about 100ms. But I am running home assistant on a quite old and slow Odroid U3 and during the startup of home assistant this machine is quite busy which may cause the commands to take longer.

I just played around with the configuration, disabled the `command_line` sensors, enabled some of them and did many restarts of home assistant. I noticed that on some restarts the `fritzbox` sensors were available but most of the time they were not. It looks like there is at most a small correlation between the availability of the `fritzbox` sensors and the `command_line` sensors. The main problem might be my slow machine. The overall startup of home assistant tooks about 2 minutes.

So making the `fritzbox` integration more robust in the setup behavior sounds good to me. :smiley:

> Under normal circumstances the commands take only about 100ms

Compared to `Setup of domain command_line took 55.8 seconds.` let me think about, what happens that it needs 100 times the duration of "normal circumstances" 🤔 

> The main problem might be my slow machine

The root cause is, that the setup of the `sensor` platform is heavily delayed by some integration. Just to make sure there are no issues with your custom integrations, please try to start HA in safe mode (_this will disable any custom components_)
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/35783820/8917226e-faa2-4171-ad42-9006b58b9056)

1. Restart in safe mode:
```
2023-12-11 22:13:30.583 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain sensor took 0.0 seconds
2023-12-11 22:13:31.057 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain command_line took 15.7 seconds
[...]
2023-12-11 22:13:47.776 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.bootstrap] Home Assistant initialized in 47.35s
```

2. Restart (in normal mode) from UI:
```
2023-12-11 22:32:38.762 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain sensor took 0.0 seconds
2023-12-11 22:32:39.126 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setting up tts
2023-12-11 22:32:39.140 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain command_line took 16.4 seconds
2023-12-11 22:32:39.151 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.fritzbox] enable smarthome templates: True
2023-12-11 22:32:39.163 INFO (SyncWorker_4) [pyfritzhome.fritzhome] Updating Devices ...
[...]
2023-12-11 22:33:07.323 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.homematicip_local.control_unit] Started central unit for RaspberryMatic
2023-12-11 22:33:07.416 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.bootstrap] Home Assistant initialized in 59.04s
```

3. Starting a fresh docker container (docker run). This is how I normally restart home assistant:
```
2023-12-11 22:41:59.750 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain sensor took 0.0 seconds
2023-12-11 22:42:00.035 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.binary_sensor] Setting up binary_sensor.homematicip_local
2023-12-11 22:42:00.039 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup of domain command_line took 56.0 seconds
[...]
2023-12-11 22:42:23.618 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.fritzbox] Finished fetching aed06adbcc1dbe9385563c2a334228b7 data in 0.993 seconds (success: True)
2023-12-11 22:42:24.109 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.homematicip_local.control_unit] Started central unit for RaspberryMatic
2023-12-11 22:42:24.773 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.bootstrap] Home Assistant initialized in 95.04s
```

Interestingly the startup of home assistant takes much longer inside of a newly created docker container (case 3). The custom integrations don't make a big difference. In the cases 1 and 2 the `fritzbox` sensors were available. In case 3 the sensors were available in about 1 restart out of 5.

If I disable my `command_line` sensors, the home assistant initialization takes also around 90s with a newly created container and around 60s if I restart it in the UI. There are no domains which take longer than 10s to set up.

when creating a new container, all python dependencies needs to be downloaded and installed again. You only need to recreate the container in case of an HA upgrade (_pull new image_). For just restarting HA it is enough to stop and start the container.

> when creating a new container, all python dependencies needs to be downloaded and installed again.

Aren't the dependencies already included in the docker image (installed during the build process of the image)? I don't see any download or install messages in the startup logs of a new HA container.

> You only need to recreate the container in case of an HA upgrade (_pull new image_). For just restarting HA it is enough to stop and start the container.

Yes, normally I only restart HA after pulling a new image. 😉

But at least now I have a workaround to see the `fritzbox` sensors again: I just have to do a restart via UI.

> Aren't the dependencies already included in the docker image (installed during the build process of the image)? I don't see any download or install messages in the startup logs of a new HA container.

There are only some basic requirements installed within the image, so that HA core can start and begin with the bootstrap process. For each used integrations, the dependencies are loaded and installed during start up (_sure, when already installed, than this is skipped_)
